meta.trial_name: GISSI-HF (Gruppo Italiano per lo Studio della Sopravvivenza nell'Insufficienza cardiaca - Heart Failure), rosuvastatin comparison (R2)
meta.drug: rosuvastatin 10 mg once daily vs placebo
meta.sponsor: Gruppo di Ricerca GISSI (ANMCO, Mario Negri institutes); funded by Societa Prodotti Antibiotici (SPA), Pfizer, Sigma Tau and AstraZeneca
meta.mechanism: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin); LDL-C about 0.92 mmol/L lower than placebo at 1 year (CTT) from a baseline of about 3.1 mmol/L
meta.indication: chronic symptomatic heart failure (NYHA II-IV) of any cause and any ejection fraction, in patients without a clear indication or contraindication for statins; outcomes all-cause death, and death or cardiovascular hospitalisation

n_randomized.quote: We enrolled patients aged 18 years or older with chronic heart failure of New York Heart Association class II-IV, irrespective of cause and left ventricular ejection fraction, and randomly assigned them to rosuvastatin 10 mg daily (n=2285) or placebo (n=2289) by a concealed, computerised telephone randomisation system. Patients were followed up for a median of 3.9 years (IQR 3.0-4.4).
n_randomized.note: Registry S3 enrolment 6975 is the whole GISSI-HF programme (n-3 PUFA comparison R1); R2 (rosuvastatin) is 4574. The 2018 AHA/ACC data supplement S6 lists 'Size: 4631 randomized' and the NERDCAT summary S19 '4631 randomized -> 4574 analyzed'; the abstract says 'We analysed all randomised patients'. Discrepancy not resolved (full text not read).

median_followup.quote: Patients were followed up for a median of 3.9 years (IQR 3.0-4.4).
median_followup.note: CTT 2010 (S5 Table 1) gives median follow-up in survivors 4.2 years; Feinstein 2015 (S7) gives 46.9 months.

primary_endpoint.value: Co-primary: (1) time to death from any cause; (2) time to death or admission to hospital for cardiovascular reasons
primary_endpoint.quote: Primary endpoints were time to death, and time to death or admission to hospital for cardiovascular reasons.
primary_endpoint.note: Same co-primary endpoints as the n-3 PUFA comparison (design paper S4). Registry S3 lists the second primary outcome as 'All cause mortality or hospitalizations for any reason' (registry wording differs from the paper).

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age >=18; chronic heart failure NYHA II-IV of any cause and any LVEF (if LVEF >40%, at least one HF admission in the previous year); no clear indication or contraindication for statins; creatinine <=2.5 mg/dL, ALT/AST <=1.5x ULN, CPK <=ULN
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Clinical evidence of heart failure according to the European Society of Cardiology guidelines (New York Heart Association class II-IV)
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Design paper S4: 'Patients with no clear indication or contraindication to cholesterol-lowering therapy will be further randomized to receive low-dose rosuvastatin (10 mg daily) or placebo.' Registry R2 exclusions: 'current serum creatinine level >2.5 mg/dL; current ALT, AST level >1.5 times the upper normal limit; current CPK upper normal limits.' Etiology (S6, S8): ischaemic 40%, dilated 34.5-35%, hypertensive 18%.

planned_events.unit: deaths (event-driven target, set for the programme)
planned_events.quote: it is expected that 70% of the patients will be suitable to enter both components of the trial, which assume the same co-primary endpoints: (a) 15% reduction of all-cause mortality and (b) 20% reduction of all-cause mortality or cardiovascular hospitalizations. The trial is event-driven and will continue either until at least 1252 deaths have been recorded or a reduction of all-cause mortality will satisfy the significance boundaries, which have been established to stop the study.
planned_events.note: Registry S3 time frame 'from enrollment to 1252 deaths in R2 arm'. Observed in R2: 657 + 644 = 1301 deaths. Read in the design-paper abstract only (full text not read).

assumed_rrr.unit: fraction (all-cause mortality); 0.20 for death or CV hospitalisation
assumed_rrr.quote: it is expected that 70% of the patients will be suitable to enter both components of the trial, which assume the same co-primary endpoints: (a) 15% reduction of all-cause mortality and (b) 20% reduction of all-cause mortality or cardiovascular hospitalizations. The trial is event-driven and will continue either until at least 1252 deaths have been recorded or a reduction of all-cause mortality will satisfy the significance boundaries, which have been established to stop the study.
assumed_rrr.note: Both components (n-3 PUFA and rosuvastatin) assumed the same effect sizes.

power.note: NOT FOUND: power is not stated in the design-paper abstract (S4) or the Lancet abstract (S1); full texts not read.

alpha.unit: two-sided for all-cause death (95.5% CI); 0.01 for death or CV hospitalisation (99% CI)
alpha.quote: 657 (29%) patients died from any cause in the rosuvastatin group and 644 (28%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.00 [95.5% CI 0.898-1.122], p=0.943).
alpha.note: DERIVED from the confidence levels reported in the abstract (95.5% CI for death, 99% CI for the combined endpoint), i.e. the overall 0.05 split between the co-primary endpoints; the exact alpha allocation text in Methods was not read.

stopped_early.quote: Patients were followed up for a median of 3.9 years (IQR 3.0-4.4).
stopped_early.note: Not stopped early; ran to completion (registry S3 primary completion 2008-04 ACTUAL, overall status COMPLETED).

baseline.quote: G1: LDL-C 3.16 mmol/L* to 2.31 mmol/L after 3 y G2: LDL-C 3.13 mmol/L to 3.06 mmol/L after 3 y.
baseline.location: Data Supplement 6, GISSI HF row (Endpoint results column)
baseline.note: Read in the 2018 AHA/ACC cholesterol guideline data supplement (evidence table abstracted from the Lancet paper; pdftotext of a multi-column table, cell text joined). CTT 2010 (S5 Table 1) gives baseline LDL-C 3.06 mmol/L for GISSI-HF from its individual-participant data. NERDCAT S19: 'LDL ~3.15, HDL 1.2 mmol/L'. Lancet Table 1 not read.
Secondary summary only (NERDCAT); primary Table 1 not read.

baseline.quote: At baseline, 50.7% of participants had an admission for heart failure in the previous year, the mean heart rate was 73 bpm, and the mean systolic blood pressure was 127 mm Hg.
baseline.note: ACC Latest in Cardiology trial summary (secondary).

biomarker_effects.method: CTT individual-participant data: LDL-C difference between arms at 1 year
biomarker_effects.location: Table 1 (columns: number of patients, treatment comparison, median follow-up in survivors (years), baseline LDL-C (mmol/L), LDL-C difference at 1 year (mmol/L))
biomarker_effects.note: Table row read in the CTT 2010 PMC XML (cells joined with ' | '). change_pct DERIVED: -0.92 / 3.06 (CTT baseline) = -30.1%. NERDCAT S19 (secondary): 'LDL reduced by ~30% in rosuvastatin group @ baseline: 3.16 mmol/L @ 1 y: 2.15 mmol/L'.

biomarker_effects.method: per-arm means as abstracted in the 2018 AHA/ACC evidence table
biomarker_effects.quote: G1: LDL-C 3.16 mmol/L* to 2.31 mmol/L after 3 y G2: LDL-C 3.13 mmol/L to 3.06 mmol/L after 3 y.
biomarker_effects.note: DERIVED: rosuvastatin 3.16 -> 2.31 (-0.85 mmol/L, -26.9%) minus placebo 3.13 -> 3.06 (-0.07, -2.2%) = -0.78 mmol/L, -24.7 percentage points. Smaller than at 1 year, consistent with about 35% permanent discontinuation in each arm. The ACC summary S10 gives conflicting values ('The mean low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) at baseline was 57 mg/dl ... At 3 years, LDL-C had decreased to 42 mg/dl'), which are inconsistent with every other source and were not used.
NOT FOUND (Lancet full text not accessible).

biomarker_effects.timepoint: CORONA (same drug and dose, ischaemic systolic HF), between-group difference
biomarker_effects.quote: patients in the rosuvastatin group had decreased levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (difference between groups, 45.0%; P<0.001) and of high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (difference between groups, 37.1%; P<0.001).
biomarker_effects.note: No GISSI-HF-specific phase 2 study exists; this is the closest pre-readout lipid evidence for rosuvastatin 10 mg in heart failure (a different phase 3 trial, used here as prior evidence).

hr.quote: 657 (29%) patients died from any cause in the rosuvastatin group and 644 (28%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.00 [95.5% CI 0.898-1.122], p=0.943).
hr.note: Unadjusted: the data supplement S6 lists 'HR: 1.03; 95% CI: 0.91-1.14' and NERDCAT 'HR 1.03 (95.5% CI 0.92-1.15)'. Co-primary 2 (death or CV hospitalisation): 1305 (57%) patients in the rosuvastatin group and 1283 (56%) in the placebo group died or were admitted to hospital for cardiovascular reasons (adjusted HR 1.01 [99% CI 0.908-1.112], p=0.903). Secondary outcomes (S6): cardiovascular mortality 478 (20.9%) vs 488 (21.3%), HR 0.98 (0.87-1.12); sudden cardiac death 220 (9.6%) vs 196 (8.6%), HR 1.13 (0.93-1.37); admission for HF 629 (27.5%) vs 634 (27.7%), HR 1.00 (0.90-1.12); fatal and non-fatal MI 61 (2.7%) vs 70 (3.1%), HR 0.88 (0.63-1.24); fatal and non-fatal stroke 82 (3.6%) vs 66 (2.9%), HR 1.25 (0.91-1.73). Per-protocol death HR 1.12 (0.97-1.29). 'No heterogeneity of effect across various subgroups.'

ci_low.quote: 657 (29%) patients died from any cause in the rosuvastatin group and 644 (28%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.00 [95.5% CI 0.898-1.122], p=0.943).

ci_high.quote: 657 (29%) patients died from any cause in the rosuvastatin group and 644 (28%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.00 [95.5% CI 0.898-1.122], p=0.943).

p.quote: 657 (29%) patients died from any cause in the rosuvastatin group and 644 (28%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.00 [95.5% CI 0.898-1.122], p=0.943).

events_treatment.quote: 657 (29%) patients died from any cause in the rosuvastatin group and 644 (28%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.00 [95.5% CI 0.898-1.122], p=0.943).
events_treatment.note: Also in ESC release S2. Combined endpoint 1305.

events_control.quote: 657 (29%) patients died from any cause in the rosuvastatin group and 644 (28%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.00 [95.5% CI 0.898-1.122], p=0.943).
events_control.note: Also in ESC release S2. Combined endpoint 1283. Total deaths 1301 (planned at least 1252).

safety_signals.value: No safety signal: gastrointestinal disorders were the most frequent adverse reaction, 34 (1%) vs 44 (2%)
safety_signals.quote: In both groups, gastrointestinal disorders were the most frequent adverse reaction (34 [1%] rosuvastatin group vs 44 [2%] placebo group).
safety_signals.note: Interpretation: 'Rosuvastatin 10 mg daily did not affect clinical outcomes in patients with chronic heart failure of any cause, in whom the drug was safe.'

safety_signals.value: Discontinuation similar: permanent discontinuation 790 (34.6%) vs 831 (36.3%); for adverse drug reaction 104 (4.6%) vs 91 (4.0%); muscle-related 23 vs 21; CK >5x ULN 9 vs 2
safety_signals.quote: Permanent discontinuation of study treatment: G1: 790 (34.6%), G2: 831 (36.3%), p=0.22 -Permanent discontinuation due to adverse drug reaction: G1: 104 (4.6%), G2: 91 (4.0%), p=0.36 -Permanent discontinuation due to muscle-related symptoms: G1: 23, G2: 21. -CK >5x ULN: G1: 9, G2: 2
safety_signals.location: Data Supplement 6, GISSI HF row (Study limitations / adverse events column)
safety_signals.note: Secondary abstraction of the Lancet paper. High discontinuation (about 35%) dilutes the intention-to-treat contrast; ACC summary S10: 'The rate of medication discontinuation was 34.6% for rosuvastatin versus 36.3% for placebo.'

safety_signals.value: Non-significant excess of stroke: 82 (3.6%) vs 66 (2.9%), HR 1.25 (0.91-1.73)
safety_signals.note: Not significant; the pooled CORONA + GISSI-HF analysis S7 found 'no significant differences between rosuvastatin and placebo in risks for stroke'.

safety_signals.value: Possible benefit on new atrial fibrillation (ancillary): 13.9% vs 16.0%, P=0.097 unadjusted, P=0.038 fully adjusted
safety_signals.quote: Among the 3690 patients (80.7%) without AF on their baseline ECG, 15.0% developed AF during a median follow-up period of 3.7 years, 258 randomized to rosuvastatin (13.9%) vs. 294 allocated to placebo (16.0%).

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: HMGCR (statin target) LDL-lowering variants protect against cardiovascular events, the same per unit LDL-C as PCSK9 variants
genetics.effect: OR 0.81 (0.72-0.90) per 10 mg/dL lower LDL-C for the HMGCR score
genetics.quote: Variants in PCSK9 and HMGCR were associated with nearly identical protective effects on the risk of cardiovascular events per decrease of 10 mg per deciliter (0.26 mmol per liter) in the LDL cholesterol level: odds ratio for cardiovascular events, 0.81 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.89) for PCSK9 and 0.81 (95% CI, 0.72 to 0.90) for HMGCR.

genetics.finding: 2x2 factorial MR: HMGCR variants lowering LDL-C by 2.9 mg/dL associated with 5.3% lower CHD risk
genetics.quote: whereas the HMGCR group had 2.9 mg/dl lower LDL-C and a similar 5.3% lower risk of CHD (OR: 0.947, 95% CI: 0.909 to 0.986).

genetics.finding: HMGCR variants lower LDL-C and slightly raise type 2 diabetes risk and bodyweight (on-target statin effect)
genetics.effect: rs17238484-G: 0.06 mmol/L lower LDL-C per allele
genetics.quote: The increased risk of type 2 diabetes noted with statins is at least partially explained by HMGCR inhibition.

genetics.finding: CTT 2005 (pre-readout benchmark): about one-fifth fewer major vascular events per 1 mmol/L LDL-C; all-cause mortality 12% lower, with non-significant effects on non-coronary vascular and non-vascular deaths
genetics.effect: RR 0.79 (0.77-0.81) major vascular events; RR 0.88 (0.84-0.91) all-cause mortality per 1.0 mmol/L
genetics.quote: There was a 12% proportional reduction in all-cause mortality per mmol/L reduction in LDL cholesterol (rate ratio [RR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.84-0.91; p<0.0001). This reflected a 19% reduction in coronary mortality (0.81, 0.76-0.85; p<0.0001), and non-significant reductions in non-coronary vascular mortality (0.93, 0.83-1.03; p=0.2) and non-vascular mortality (0.95, 0.90-1.01; p=0.1).

genetics.finding: CTT 2010 (includes GISSI-HF): RR 0.78 per 1 mmol/L for major vascular events; all-cause mortality RR 0.90 per 1 mmol/L
genetics.effect: RR 0.78 (0.76-0.80) MVE; RR 0.90 (0.87-0.93) all-cause death per 1.0 mmol/L
genetics.quote: Across all 26 trials, all-cause mortality was reduced by 10% per 1·0 mmol/L LDL reduction (RR 0·90, 95% CI 0·87–0·93; p<0·0001), largely reflecting significant reductions in deaths due to coronary heart disease (RR 0·80, 99% CI 0·74–0·87; p<0·0001) and other cardiac causes (RR 0·89, 99% CI 0·81–0·98; p=0·002)

genetics.finding: EAS consensus: LDL causes atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
genetics.quote: Consistent evidence from numerous and multiple different types of clinical and genetic studies unequivocally establishes that LDL causes ASCVD.

consensus_explanation.summary: Rosuvastatin 10 mg lowered LDL-C by about 0.9 mmol/L (about 30%) at 1 year, but did not change all-cause death (HR 1.00, 95.5% CI 0.898-1.122; 1301 deaths) or death/cardiovascular hospitalisation (HR 1.01) in 4574 patients with chronic heart failure of any cause. Experts did not doubt that LDL or HMGCR is causal for atherosclerosis; they concluded that in heart failure most deaths and admissions come from pump failure and arrhythmia, which LDL lowering does not prevent. CTT 2010, which included GISSI-HF, noted that most cardiac deaths in GISSI-HF and CORONA were non-occlusive, and the pooled CORONA + GISSI-HF reanalysis found a small but significant reduction in myocardial infarction in ischaemic heart failure (HR 0.81, 0.66-0.99), which was swamped by competing non-atherothrombotic deaths. Reviews add that GISSI-HF enrolled many non-ischaemic patients at low atherosclerotic risk (only 40% ischaemic), and that the all-cause endpoint, about 35% discontinuation and a single low-dose hydrophilic statin limit the conclusions. The discussant called statins' pleiotropic effects clinically irrelevant in heart failure, and guidelines do not recommend starting statins for heart failure alone.

pre_readout.note: Facts with a public source dated before readout_date (2008-08-31).
available_before_readout: Design paper (S4, 2004-08): co-primary endpoints, assumed 15% mortality and 20% death/CV-hospitalisation reductions, event-driven to at least 1252 deaths, rosuvastatin arm limited to patients without clear indication/contraindication for statins
Registry record (S3, first posted 2006-06-13): eligibility (any LVEF, any cause), R2 exclusions, co-primary outcomes
CORONA (S11, 2007-11-05): rosuvastatin 10 mg in older ischaemic systolic HF lowered LDL-C 45% but did not reduce CV death/MI/stroke (HR 0.92, 0.83-1.02) or death (HR 0.95)
CTT 2005 (S12, 2005-09-27): about 21% fewer major vascular events and 12% lower all-cause mortality per 1 mmol/L LDL-C, mainly coronary deaths
only_after_readout: Outcome HRs, events, safety (S1 and ESC release S2, 2008-08-31)
Fonarow Lancet comment (S14), MDedge report with discussant comments (S9, 2008-10-01), ESC trials update (S20, 2008-11-12)
AF ancillary analysis (S13, 2009-08-30); CTT 2010 Table 1 LDL-C difference and the non-occlusive cardiac death interpretation (S5, 2010-11-08)
Pooled CORONA + GISSI-HF reanalysis (S7, 2015-02-14); 2018 AHA/ACC evidence tables (S6); reviews (S21 2013, S8 2026)
HMGCR genetics (S15 2015, S16 2016, S17 2014) and EAS consensus (S18, 2017)

access_summary.note: Key numbers: n, median FU, planned events, assumed RRR, power, alpha, baseline LDL-C/HDL-C/TG/apoB, LDL-C % and abs change, non-HDL-C change, apoB change, HR, CI low/high, p, events x2. The Lancet paper S1 is paywalled (thelancet.com 'Log in, subscribe or purchase for full access'; Wayback captures 2009/2011 show the same paywall; Unpaywall/Semantic Scholar list no open copy): n, median FU, HR, CI, p and events come from its free abstract (identical in the ESC release S2). Planned events and assumed RRR come from the design-paper abstract S4. LDL-C 1-year difference from CTT 2010 Table 1 (S5, open full text). Baseline LDL-C and the 3-year LDL-C values come from the 2018 AHA/ACC evidence table S6 (open PDF, secondary abstraction), baseline HDL-C from a blog summary S19. Not found: power, baseline TG/apoB, apoB, non-HDL-C and hsCRP changes. Counted: open_full_text = LDL-C abs and % change (S5), baseline LDL-C (S6, secondary) and HDL-C (S19, secondary); abstract_only = n, FU, planned events, RRR, alpha (derived), HR, CI low/high, p, events x2 (S1/S4; HR, CI, p and events also in the press release S2); not_found = power, baseline TG, baseline apoB, non-HDL-C change, apoB change.

sources.note: CTT Collaboration, Lancet 2010;376:1670-81. Full text read via NCBI efetch (PMC XML). Table 1 GISSI-HF row read. Discussion: 'For example, in the GISSI-HF trial of rosuvastatin versus placebo in patients with heart failure (which was included in this meta-analysis), as well as in the similar CORONA trial (which was not), most cardiac deaths were non-occlusive and there were no significant reductions in cardiac mortality.' and 'This finding may reflect a relative lack of benefit from lowering of LDL cholesterol on cardiac deaths that are mediated by non-occlusive mechanisms.'

sources.title: Statin Therapy Offers No Benefit in Chronic Heart Failure
sources.note: Bruce Jancin, MDedge Internal Medicine, October 1, 2008 (ESC congress report). Read via curl. Discussant: 'Discussant Dr. Philip Poole-Wilson commented that he found GISSI-HF persuasive and generalizable, particularly taken together with CORONA. The findings are surprising and disappointing in light of the much-discussed pleiotropic effects of statins, which now appear to be clinically irrelevant in the setting of heart failure.' Also: 'The GISSI-HF trial indicates patients with symptomatic heart failure should not be started on a statin.'

'GISSI-HF, on the other hand, may have washed out any effect in ischemic HFrEF by also enrolling patients with no CAD and at low risk for an atherosclerotic CV event.' Used only for corroboration (1-year LDL-C 2.15 mmol/L, 4631 randomized -> 4574 analyzed, HDL-C 1.2).

sources.title: Clinical trials update from European Society of Cardiology meeting 2008: TIME-CHF, BACH, BEAUTIFUL, GISSI-HF, and HOME-HF
sources.note: Coletta AP, Cullington D, Clark AL, Cleland JG. Eur J Heart Fail 2008;10:1264-7. Abstract read: 'In GISSI-HF, n-3 PUFA reduced mortality and cardiovascular hospitalisation by a small amount compared to placebo in patients with chronic heart failure, but rosuvastatin had no effect on clinical outcomes.' Full commentary not read (Wiley 403).

sources.title: Statins in heart failure: do we need another trial?
sources.note: Bonsu KO, Kadirvelu A, Reidpath DD. Vasc Health Risk Manag 2013;9:303-19. Full text read via NCBI efetch: 'The CORONA and GISSI-HF studies assessed the effect of one type of statin at a low dose, thus the insignificant results provide inconclusive evidence for the class effect of statins in HF.' Also argues rosuvastatin is hydrophilic with 'very low uptake by cardiac muscles'.

open_questions: Category: population (primary), design_or_endpoint (secondary). CTT 2010 (S5) attributes the null result in GISSI-HF and CORONA to mostly non-occlusive cardiac deaths, which LDL lowering does not prevent; the pooled CORONA + GISSI-HF reanalysis (S7) found fewer MIs in ischaemic HF but competing non-atherothrombotic deaths; reviews (S8, S19) stress competing pump-failure/arrhythmic risk and the inclusion of non-ischaemic, low-atherosclerotic-risk patients. design_or_endpoint is secondary: an all-cause death endpoint and about 35% discontinuation dilute any atherosclerotic benefit, and critics (S10, S21) note that only one low-dose hydrophilic statin was tested. effect_too_small is a weaker alternative: with about -0.92 mmol/L LDL-C and CTT's all-cause RR 0.90 per mmol/L, the expected HR for death is about 0.91 (derived, not from a source), close to the lower CI bound 0.898, so the trial had limited power for an LDL-mediated mortality effect even in a typical population.

Lancet full text (S1) was not accessible (paywall): Table 1 baselines, on-treatment lipid and hsCRP values, the power statement and the exact alpha allocation were NOT verified in the primary source. Baseline LDL-C 3.16 mmol/L and 3-year values come from the 2018 AHA/ACC evidence table (S6); the 1-year LDL-C difference -0.92 mmol/L comes from CTT 2010 (S5), whose baseline (3.06 mmol/L) differs from the paper's arm mean (3.16).
Randomized count: abstract 4574 ('We analysed all randomised patients'), but S6 and S19 list 4631 randomized; not resolved.
Adjusted vs unadjusted death HR: abstract adjusted HR 1.00 (95.5% CI 0.898-1.122); S6 lists HR 1.03 (0.91-1.14) and S19 HR 1.03 (95.5% CI 0.92-1.15), presumably unadjusted.
Registry S3 words the second primary outcome as 'All cause mortality or hospitalizations for any reason', while the paper and press release use cardiovascular hospitalisation.
ACC summary S10 gives baseline LDL-C 57/56 mg/dL and 42 mg/dL at 3 years, inconsistent with S5, S6 and S19; treated as an error.

Topline release S2: the ESC page for 31 Aug 2008 is read through the earliest Wayback capture (2008-10-10); the builder's web.archive.org/web/20080831/<url> lookup redirects there and returns the full text. The Lancet paper went online the same day (cited as 'published online Aug 31'), although PubMed lists an electronic date of 2008-08-29.
Fonarow's Lancet comment (S14) and the Cleland ESC update (S20) were read only partially (first paragraph / abstract).
